conventions: בְּ standing on a temporal adverb and rendered by one English word fuses with it under rule 30 and heads on the adverb: בְּעוֹד → While (39.1), בְּטֶרֶם → Before (39.13). The competing reading, the word on the בְּ under rule 52 with the adverb unrepresented, was considered and set aside for both.

The ASV's 'held my peace' / 'Hold thy peace' for חָשָׁה and חָרֵשׁ is one idiomatic rendering of the verb: the possessive is part of the idiom and stays in the verb's unit, headed on 'peace' (rules 30, 44), not added under rule 18 (39.2, 39.12).

A bare Hebrew direct object the ASV demotes to a 'with' instrument while the verb stays an English verb with a promoted object gives the 'with' to the verb (rule 33 direct-object paragraph, PRO.7.16 shape): 39.1 'keep my mouth with a bridle'. A genuine adverbial accusative keeps its supplied preposition (39.2 'with silence', 39.5 'as handbreadths', 39.6 'in vain').
report: Read all 19 candidate groups end to end. Every difference in the suffix, waw, בְּ, לְ, מִן, כֹּל, הֶבֶל, אַיִן, הִיא, כְּ and מָה buckets is licensed by the source or by the ASV's own wording (tripartite resumptive הִיא in 39.7 vs explicit subject in 39.4; אֲדֹנָי's lexicalized suffix in 39.7; unrendered apodosis waw in 39.11; substantival אַיִן in 39.5 vs existential in 39.13). No cross-verse split.

The chapter's recurring constructions are consistent: בְּ fused with a following temporal adverb into one English word (39.1 בְּעוֹד → While, 39.13 בְּטֶרֶם → Before, both headed on the adverb); the 'held my peace' / 'Hold thy peace' idiom carrying its own possessive inside the verb's unit (39.2, 39.12); a supplied preposition the English verb needs to reach a bare Hebrew object joining the verb (39.1 take heed to, 39.7 wait for, 39.12 give ear unto).

One within-verse correction, PSA.39.1: מַחְסוֹם is the direct object of אֶשְׁמְרָה in the Hebrew and the ASV keeps that verb a verb while demoting the object to an instrument ('keep my mouth with a bridle'); rule 33's closing paragraph and its PRO.7.16 precedent ('I have spread my couch with carpets') give such a 'with' to the verb, not to the noun. Moved 'with' from the noun's unit to the verb's (discontinuous, rule 25); the noun keeps 'a bridle'.
The five added units (39.3 Then, 39.6 riches, 39.9 it, 39.11 When, 39.13 hence) were each checked against the morphemes in their clauses; none is folded elsewhere in another verse.

BSB disagreements are all documented convention differences (recasting-silenced לְ/מִן, paragogic he/nun, rule 57 suffix, rule 50 suffix on אַיִן, tripartite resumptive pronoun, unrendered apodosis waw). None is a genuine error.
No contract promotion or amendment: nothing this chapter taught is more general than the rules already state.
